One-screen UI, second pass: before and after

2026-09-30 · the ten ideas from the second "consolidate the phone UI" list, all built. Every picture is a real capture from the editor at the phone's own 1080 × 1920 (training/tools/ui_shots.sh), game camera and every UI panel together.

How to read this. Red dashed boxes on the left are what was wrong; orange boxes on the right are what changed, numbered to the notes under each pair. Race pictures read 200 FPS because the editor is stepped one physics tick at a time to take them. The before results picture is yesterday's capture of the same code: this morning's attempt was spoiled by another session playing races in the same editor at the same time.

1 · The race: one line on top, four rows of order, one card at the bottom

Before

After

  • AThe event, the leader and a 74 px clock took two lines and 148 px.
  • BAll eight runners, 492 px of the top half of the picture, while the map beside it already shows everybody.
  • CThe commentary floated mid-picture on its own band.
  • DSix buttons, and RESTART was the bright green one: one stray tap mid-race threw the race away.
  • 1One line: stage, who leads, clock. 96 px.
  • 2Four rows: the leaders, and the athlete on camera on the last row when they are further back. "+4 more" opens all of them.
  • 3The caption is now the first line of the one card at the bottom.
  • 4Four buttons: CHAOS (opens GUST / SHOVE / SLICK), AUTO, RESTART (plain, asks SURE? mid-race), STATS.

2 · STATS: on the card, about the athlete you are watching

Before

After

  • EThe caption was about Grandpa…
  • F…while the stats strip underneath was always about Matt RL, the reference athlete. Two panels, two different athletes, both printing speed and distance.
  • 5One card: caption, the athlete on camera (place, speed, distance, strain).
  • 6STATS adds one line for that same athlete: the policy driving it, its state, how upright it is, the attempt.

3 · New: the CHAOS row, and locking the cameras onto a runner

CHAOS pressed

A name tapped

  • 7GUST, SHOVE and SLICK pop up above the row, count down their cooldowns as before, and put themselves away six seconds after the last use.
  • 8Tap a name in the running order and the cameras follow that runner; the row gets an amber edge.
  • 9The card says LOCKED. Tap the card again to hand the cameras back to the director. A fall elsewhere still takes the picture for the incident.
  • 10"+4 more" opened the whole order; "show fewer" puts it back to four.

4 · Results: fallers on one line, each finisher's race under their name, SHARE

Before (same race)

After

  • GFour full rows of "DNF fell at … m, 0 pts".
  • HThe highlight clip was a file name on a line.
  • 11Each finisher's top speed and the work its joints did in this race (and how often it got back up, when it did), which used to be only on the diagnostics sheet.
  • 12Everybody out on one line, in their own colours, with where they went down.
  • 13SHARE: on Android the clip goes into the gallery (Pictures/PoDecath) and the share sheet opens; on a PC the clips folder opens. The Android path has not been run on a phone yet.

5 · Setup: no heading block, faces on the tiles

Before

After

  • I"EVENT SETUP", a sentence and an EVENT label: about 300 px saying what the highlighted button already says.
  • JEach tile was a name, a big 1 and two steppers; nothing showed who the athlete was.
  • K"-- FPS" in red before the first reading looked like a fault.
  • 14The event's own note, one line under the buttons.
  • 15The athlete's face (rendered from their own model), name, and best time in the picked event. Tap the tile to add one; minus top left; the count top right; i turns it over.
  • 16START says how many are going: "8 of 16 runners".
  • 17The frame-rate chip is 300 px instead of 440 and grey until it has a reading. DEBUG's grade is now a coloured dot.

6 · Setup: an athlete's record, on the back of the tile

Before

After

  • 18Same record as before (races, wins, podiums, falls, top speed, work, best marks), now over the face; the name stays underneath and the i turns it back.

7 · Diagnostics: one LIVE page instead of AGENTS + FRAME

Before: AGENTS

Before: FRAME

After: LIVE

  • LA three-line warning across the top of the list.
  • MHalf the page empty.
  • NCLOSE, although DEBUG already closes the sheet.
  • OThe frame numbers were a separate page.
  • 19Two tabs, LIVE and SETTINGS, and EXPORT as an icon.
  • 20One summary line, coloured by how the field is doing.
  • 21A "!" on each athlete whose card has something to act on; its sentence is on its card, one tap away.
  • 22The frame graph and every counter, four across, in the space that was empty. They step aside while an athlete's card is open.

8 · Added later the same day: the last 20% of a race is a close-up of the leader

60% of the race: the usual trackside shot

86%: the leader, close up

  • 23From 80% of the distance until the race is over the camera sits about 4 m in front of whoever is leading, in their lane, at chest height, aimed straight at them. Falls no longer cut away from it. Earlier in the race a fall is shown close up on the faller for five seconds instead of on the stadium wide shot (40 m back, 30 m up), which showed the roof rather than the runners.

What is not verified

  • SHARE on Android: written against the Android API (MediaStore + share sheet), compiled, and the button works on the PC, but it has not been pressed on a phone. The next APK is the test.
  • Taps: every new control was driven by calling its code in the captures (lock, open order, CHAOS, STATS, flip). The taps themselves go through the same handlers, but nobody has tapped them with a finger yet.

Files, and the ten items with their measured results, are listed in DOCS/README.md, section "One-screen UI, second pass, 2026-09-30".
